## Exercises (sample)

1. Mapping classes/fields to tables/columns and generating routine CRUD SQL (and later relationships).
2. **Contract / specification.** Hibernate (or another provider) is the engine.
3. The entity is managed; dirty checking writes the UPDATE on flush/commit.
4. Lets Hibernate create/alter tables from entity mappings (learning convenience).

## Self-check

1. `@Entity`.
2. `persist(...)`.
3. **False.** Hibernate generates SQL from mappings and operations.
4. So the provider can create instances when loading rows from the database.
